Under data protection principles, location-based identifiers that can narrow down to a small set of individuals should be generalized or pseudonymized.

The substation identifier, while at a higher aggregation level than feeder, still serves as a geographic quasi-identifier. When combined with feeder and date, it can pinpoint a specific distribution area. In data protection frameworks, infrastructure identifiers that map to specific geographic zones are considered indirect identifiers that should be pseudonymized to prevent re-identification of consumers within that zone.
